rows.name: commit_generated.py semantics
rows.repo: tnr-tools@305a28f992e33194fbba279a3f32e698dfb2b67f (planning branch eab1f9b is identical for every cited file; only docs/forge_next/** differ)
rows.contract: Requires GITHUB_REF_TYPE=branch; `git add -- <pathspecs>`; exits 0 with 'no generated changes' when nothing staged; commits as github-actions[bot]; `git push origin HEAD:<branch>`; on failure: fetch +refs/heads/<branch>, `git rebase origin/<branch>`; conflict -> rebase --abort, exit 1; at most 3 pushes / 2 rebases.
rows.race: Handles concurrent advances of main only when the generated commit touches disjoint paths; a same-path conflict aborts (job red, nothing pushed).

rows.name: Forge Github.put (contents API)
rows.repo: tnr-tools@305a28f992e33194fbba279a3f32e698dfb2b67f (planning branch eab1f9b is identical for every cited file; only docs/forge_next/** differ)
rows.contract: GET contents/<path>?ref=main for the existing sha; PUT {message, content(b64 utf8), branch:'main', sha?}; accepts 200/201; message 'results: <name> (forge)'; only path ever written = harvests/inbox/tnr_results_<ms>.json; PAT read from localStorage tnr_bk_gh_v1 and sent only to api.github.com; without PAT or on failure the bundle is shown for manual export.
rows.race: GitHub creates the single-file commit on top of whatever main is at that instant; it cannot conflict with any other path, and the ms-timestamp filename makes same-path collisions practically impossible. It does NOT rebase or retry.

rows.name: race: Forge PUT vs answers.yml auto-commit
rows.repo: tnr-tools@305a28f992e33194fbba279a3f32e698dfb2b67f (planning branch eab1f9b is identical for every cited file; only docs/forge_next/** differ)
rows.contract: Forge PUT lands -> answers.yml (paths harvests/**) starts on that SHA -> build_answers -> commit_generated push of answers/*.
rows.race: If a second Forge PUT lands during the run, the push is rejected, commit_generated rebases (answers/* vs harvests/inbox/* are disjoint -> succeeds) and pushes; the second PUT also queued a new answers run whose concurrency group cancels the first if still running - cancellation before push loses nothing (the new run regenerates from the newer tree); cancellation after push is moot. Net: eventually consistent, no data loss; worst case one redundant regeneration.

rows.name: race: Forge PUT vs release_pin.yml / skillpack.yml / regen_schemas.yml
rows.repo: tnr-tools@305a28f992e33194fbba279a3f32e698dfb2b67f (planning branch eab1f9b is identical for every cited file; only docs/forge_next/** differ)
rows.contract: Each of these commits only its own generated paths (loaders; dist/* + three root files; state/schema_sentinel.json + docs/DRIFT.md).
rows.race: All disjoint from harvests/inbox, so the rebase-retry path succeeds; concurrency groups are per-workflow, not global, so up to four bot writers plus Forge/Builder PUTs can interleave, each protected only by the 3-attempt retry. Three or more competing pushes inside one retry window would fail a bot job (job red, re-runnable).

notes: Bundle-shape change hazards: harvest.py detects a bundle by top-level `captures` list + (`builder` key or a capture `proc`); `cfg:'forge'` or any entry `forgeState` flips fail-closed verify rules; forge bundles must carry `outcome:'success'`; entries need state/verdict/asserted; captures need proc/input/ok and, for any downstream data use, a list `data`. forge/test/harvest.test.mjs runs the REAL harvest.py over exported bundles (7 tests), so a Forge Next shape change must keep those green or change harvest.py in the same Lane A branch (forge.yml triggers on harvest.py too).

Live defect 1 (Behaviour-proven): Forge bundles emit `checks: null`; validate.py --parity does set(bundle.get('checks', [])) and crashes with TypeError; session_close.py --guards runs parity on the lexically newest harvests/inbox bundle, so the session-close guard goes red whenever a Forge bundle is newest (reproduced against tnr_results_1789124514980.json). Forge Next should emit a real `checks` inventory or parity must skip cfg:'forge'.

Live defect 2 (Behaviour-proven): forge/test/release_loader.test.mjs:47-51 demands exactly one @x-release-pending marker in the committed loader; after release promotion (d1dbecc) there is none, so `npm test` fails 1/293 (test 178) and forge.yml is red on main for every push in its path list. This must be fixed before CI can certify Forge Next work.

Forge cannot feed answers/, catalog_sync.py or profile_derive.py: summary captures carry only a row COUNT, full captures are restricted to seven point-read procedures (never getAllNames/getAll) and 512 KiB per body. The repository's live-name lookup layer (answers/hot.json, 27 delta rows today) still depends on Builder captures (last jutsu feed tnr_results_1788065642059, quest tnr_results_1788996474057). Forge Next needs either a reviewed widening of FULL_PERSIST_PATHS to list procedures or a names-harvest output that build_answers.py can read (list of {id|userId, name|username, hidden}).

Forge entries omit `pushed`/`live`; harvest.py diff is empty for Forge bundles and the ''<->null server-normalisation reclassification can never apply, so such a normalisation would surface as a hard FAIL (Inferred).

Manifest dialect disagreements Forge Next must decide on: legacy `jutsu` array (Builder+Forge yes, validate.py no); `select` (Builder only, Forge drops silently); `persist` (Forge only, validate.py/Builder never check); `readBack:false` (Builder honours, Forge refuses); `skipPreflight` (Builder bypasses all lints, Forge ignores, validate.py warns); entity `gameAsset` (validate.py/factory ok, Forge rejects); entity `bloodline` (Forge only); missing entity defaults to jutsu in Forge; slot `update` (Builder header dialect, Forge rejects); aiProfile create (Forge refuses); `.zip` push packs (Builder picker only); unknown procedures such as combat.getBattleHistory (Builder sends, Forge throws) - push/05 and push/06 are therefore Builder-only manifests.

Repository writes: Forge's only write is harvests/inbox/tnr_results_<ms>.json via a non-retrying, sha-aware contents-API PUT to main; Builder additionally offers an arbitrary-directory file commit (default state/). Workflow-owned paths (answers/*, dist/*, root 45c/45g/32b, both loaders, state/schema_sentinel.json, docs/DRIFT.md) are regenerated by commit_generated.py and would silently overwrite any Forge-written content. A new approval-state file is safest under state/** or push/** (only scrub fires); anything under harvests/** fires answers.yml, skills/** fires skillpack (2 MiB zip cap + four coherence gates), forge/** fires forge.yml, root bundle names fire release_pin. Workflow files themselves cannot be written by the container PAT (staged under state/staged_workflows/, installed by the user).

Roadmap contract for an app: roadmap.json is single-line JSON with no enforced formatting; any write must satisfy content_workstream.py validate (status enums, dependency-satisfaction, evidence anchors that already exist in the tree, lowercase 40-hex SHAs, no sandbox/absolute paths, resume_note on IN_PROGRESS, empty evidence on PLANNED) and must be followed by `render --all` or `render --check` fails; none of this is enforced in CI. Roadmap resources/evidence cite specific harvests/inbox bundles, so inbox compaction must not delete cited bundles.

Release contract for a bigger Forge: one @require per loader naming forge_bundle.js on jsDelivr at a 40-hex SHA, @version == forge/package.json except when staged with @x-release-pending, @updateURL/@downloadURL fixed to raw main; forge.yml requires the committed forge_bundle.js to be byte-identical to `npm run build` (esbuild 0.28.2, single IIFE, innerHTML forbidden) and fixtures regenerated identically. A multi-file or renamed bundle changes pin_release.py TARGETS, release_pin.yml paths, check_release_pin.mjs (file name + first-@require parsing), forge.yml verify step, build.mjs and the loader. jsDelivr per-file limits and ViolentMonkey multi-@require behaviour were not verified (Assumed).

Shared browser state: tnr_bk_gh_v1 (PAT/sync flag) and tnr_bk_idmap_v1 (srcId->id, @img->url) are read by both Builder and Forge on the same origin; Forge Next changing either format breaks the other tool for that operator.

Scope/evidence note: every citation is from the tnr-tools checkout at main 305a28f (branch eab1f9b differs only under docs/forge_next/**). No game-source checkout was needed for this consumer/producer map; the only engine-pin facts referenced are the ones Forge itself embeds (forge/build.mjs:17 and forge/src/runner/fields.json _provenance = 345d18ac). Repo left untouched (git status clean after all runs; build_answers output went to the scratchpad).
